extracted.intended_audience: State educational agencies (SEAs), local educational agencies (LEAs), grant applicants, and education policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize eligibility, allocation, use-of-funds, priorities, matching, reporting, evaluation, and program-specific requirements for federal K–12 education grant programs under ESSA. Intended to guide SEAs/LEAs and applicants in applying for and administering grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: RLIS LEA eligibility — child-poverty rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible LEAs must have a Census child-poverty rate of at least 20 percent.

rubrics_metrics.name: RLIS LEA eligibility — NCES locale codes
rubrics_metrics.description: LEAs must serve only schools that have an NCES locale code of 32 (Town, Distant), 33 (Town, Remote), 41 (Rural, Fringe), 42 (Rural, Distant), or 43 (Rural, Remote).

rubrics_metrics.name: RLIS state allocation options to LEAs
rubrics_metrics.description: States have three options for allocating funds to eligible LEAs: competitively; through a formula based on the number of children in average daily attendance (ADA) in eligible LEAs within the State; or an alternative formula if the state can demonstrate that it would better target funds to eligible LEAs that serve the highest concentrations of poor students.

rubrics_metrics.name: RLIS permitted uses of funds (authorized programs)
rubrics_metrics.description: LEAs may use program funds to carry out activities authorized under Part A of Title I, Part A of Title II, Part A of Title III, Part A of Title IV, and parental involvement activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed include Improving Basic Programs Operated by LEAs; Supporting Effective Instruction State Grants; English Language Acquisition State Grants; Student Support and Academic Enrichment State Grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: RLIS program purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: to assist rural school districts in carrying out activities to help improve the quality of teaching and learning in their schools; provides funds to rural LEAs that serve high concentrations of poor students, regardless of the LEA’s size.

rubrics_metrics.name: RLIS program changes under ESSA (administrative/eligibility changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program changes include: updates to locale codes used for determining eligibility; extension to RLIS of the alternative State certification option for meeting the rural criterion; option for an LEA eligible for both SRSA and RLIS to choose which program to receive funds under; expanded State RLIS application requirements; and updated accountability provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian Education eligibility (LEAs/BIE/schools/tribes/orgs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility for grants to LEAs or Bureau of Indian Education schools, Indian tribes, Indian organizations, or Indian community-based organizations is tied to numbers or shares of American Indian/Alaska Native children (text lists '# of American Indian/Alaska Native children' and 'of total enrollment'). Some LEAs are exempt (LEAs in Alaska, California, and Oklahoma, and those located on or near reservations). LEAs may form a consortium to obtain grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page shows two threshold columns (# of Indian children and percent of total enrollment) but specific numeric thresholds are indicated elsewhere in statute; here the rubric identifies that eligibility is based on counts or shares of American Indian/Alaska Native students and lists specified exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian Education formula allocation (APPE or 80% US APPE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formula allocates grants using the average per pupil expenditure (APPE) in the LEA’s state or 80% of the US APPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum allocation for an LEA is $3,000. If appropriations are insufficient, amounts determined by the formula must be ratably reduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian Education minimum allocation and ratable reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum allocation for an LEA: $3,000. Ratable reductions apply if sums appropriated are insufficient to pay amounts determined for LEAs according to the formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian Education application and comprehensive plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant must annually develop and submit to the Secretary a comprehensive plan for meeting the needs of Indian children; the plan must be developed in collaboration with a local committee comprised primarily of parents and family members of Indian children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan must include student performance goals, explanation of how it will assess and report students’ progress toward meeting these goals, and a description of proposed professional development activities. Before submission to the Secretary, an LEA must submit the application to the SEA, which may comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: ED national reservations (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Education Department reserves 0.1 percent of available funds for the Outlying Areas, 1 percent for the Bureau of Indian Education, and may reserve funds to provide technical assistance and conduct evaluation and dissemination activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education for Homeless Children & Youths — formula to states
rubrics_metrics.description: After reserving funds for national set-asides, ED allocates remaining funds to States by formula based on each State's share of funds under Title I, Part A of ESEA; however a State may not receive less than $150,000; 0.25 percent of the total program appropriation for the fiscal year; or the State’s FY2001 allocation, whichever is greatest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education for Homeless — State use and reserve caps
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving its allocation, a State may reserve up to 25 percent (or, in the case of a State receiving the minimum award, 50 percent) of its allocation for State-level activities, and then must distribute remaining funds to LEAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State-level activities up to 25%; Subgrants to LEAs at least 75% (subject to minimum-award exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Education for Homeless — subgrant awarding to LEAs
rubrics_metrics.description: A State awards subgrants to LEAs competitively on the basis of need for a term not to exceed 3 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education for Homeless — permitted local uses of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: LEAs may use subgrant funds for activities such as providing enriched supplemental instruction, transportation, professional development, referrals to health care, and other services to facilitate the enrollment, attendance, and success in school of homeless children, including preschool-aged children, and youth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher and School Leader Incentive Grants — definition of human capital management systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Human capital management systems are systems by which an LEA makes and implements human capital decisions (hiring, professional development, dismissal, tenure, promotion) that include a performance-based compensation system which differentiates compensation in part on measurable increases in student academic achievement; may include differentiated pay for hard-to-staff schools/subjects and recognition for additional responsibilities and professional achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher and School Leader Incentive Grants — purpose and eligible entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: to help eligible entities develop, implement, improve, or expand human capital management systems or performance-based compensation systems in schools served by grantees. Eligible applicants: LEAs (including charter school LEAs), SEAs or other State agencies, the Bureau of Indian Education, and partnerships of LEAs/State agencies/BIE with nonprofit or for-profit entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher and School Leader Incentive Grants — priority and distribution goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority applications: Secretary is required to give priority to applicants that support teachers, principals, and other school leaders in high-need schools and to ensure an equitable geographic distribution of grants, including between rural and urban areas. High-need schools are defined (statute): public schools in which at least 30 percent of students are from low-income families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher and School Leader Incentive Grants — duration, renewals, and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration of grant awards: up to 3 years, with option of renewal for an additional 1 or 2 years if grantee demonstrates success. An LEA may receive a grant under this program only twice (whether individually or as part of a consortium).

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher and School Leader Incentive Grants — matching requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees must provide matching funds, in cash or in kind, from non-Federal sources equal to 50 percent of the amount of their grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher and School Leader Incentive Grants — required collaboration in use of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of funds: grant funds must be used in collaboration with teachers, principals, other school leaders, and members of the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive Literacy Development Grants — SEA reservation and subgrant requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An SEA may reserve up to 5 percent of its allocation for activities related to implementing its comprehensive literacy plan and administering subgrants. All remaining funds (at least 95 percent) must be used to make competitive subgrants to one or more LEAs or, for early literacy services, to one or more early childhood education programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive Literacy — subgrant distribution by grade span
rubrics_metrics.description: SEAs are required to ensure at least 15 percent of subgranted funds are used to serve children from birth through age 5; 40 percent to serve students in kindergarten through grade 5; and 40 percent to serve students in grades 6 through 12. States must equitably distribute funds among grades within the K–5 and 6–12 spans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive Literacy — national reservations and priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary must reserve one-half of 1 percent for the Department of the Interior to carry out literacy programs in BIE-funded schools; one-half of 1 percent for the Outlying Areas; may reserve up to 5 percent for national activities. Priority in awarding grants to SEAs is given to SEAs that will use funds for evidence-based activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive Literacy — eligible subgrantees and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: LEAs or early childhood education programs that receive subgrants must serve a high percentage of disadvantaged children (e.g., low-income, children with disabilities, English learners) and represent diverse geographical areas. Early childhood programs must have a demonstrated record of providing comprehensive literacy instruction for children aged birth through 5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duration: grants for up to 5 years; may be renewed for an additional 2-year period if grantee meets Secretary's terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative Approaches to Literacy — eligibility threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility: program may award grants to one or more LEAs in which at least 20 percent of the students are from low-income families; the Bureau of Indian Education; or eligible national non-profit organizations to promote literacy programs in low-income communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative Approaches to Literacy — permitted uses of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of funds: develop or enhance existing school library programs (professional learning for librarians, refreshing library materials in high-need schools); support early literacy services including outreach to parents; distribute high-quality books to children and adolescents to increase reading motivation and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: American History and Civics Academies — eligible applicants and priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants: institutions of higher education and nonprofit educational organizations, museums, libraries, research centers with demonstrated expertise, or consortia of these entities. The Secretary may make no more than 12 grants per fiscal year and must give priority for Presidential Academies grants to applicants that propose to use National Parks resources and coordinate with the National Park Service National Centennial Parks initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matching requirements: grantees must provide matching funds in an amount equal to 100 percent of the grant amount. Duration: up to 5 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: American History and Civics — program types and activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds support Presidential Academies for teachers, Congressional Academies for students, secondary school student activities, and national activities to promote evidence-based instructional methods and professional development in history/civics, with emphasis on benefiting low-income and underserved students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presidential Academies: workshops of at least 2 weeks for 50–300 teachers, with fixed stipend based on length.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEED — eligible applicants and priority criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants: institutions of higher education (IHEs), national nonprofit entities, Bureau of Indian Education, or partnerships of IHEs and national nonprofits with for-profit entities. Priority: Secretary must give priority to eligible entities that will implement evidence-based activities; ensure grants are distributed among geographically diverse areas (urban/suburban/rural) where practicable; no entity may receive more than one grant in a single competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEED — duration and matching
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration: grants may be awarded for up to 3 years and may be renewed for one additional 2-year period if grantee demonstrates success. Matching requirements: grantees must use non-Federal sources, in cash or in kind, to cover at least 25 percent of project costs each year. Secretary may waive or modify cost-sharing for demonstrated financial hardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEED — permissible purposes and required focus areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose includes: (1) supporting pathways for teachers/principals/school leaders with nontraditional preparation to obtain employment in underserved LEAs; (2) providing evidence-based PD addressing literacy, numeracy, remedial education; (3) PD to improve instruction in dual enrollment/early college; (4) making services freely available, including via public electronic means; (5) providing evidence-based professional enhancement that may lead to advanced credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: School Leader Recruitment and Support — eligible applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants: LEAs that serve high-need schools, SEAs, and the Bureau of Indian Education, or those entities in consortia with nonprofit organizations or institutions of higher education.

rubrics_metrics.name: School Leader Recruitment and Support — matching and priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Matching requirements: grantees must use non-Federal sources, in cash or in kind, to cover at least 25 percent of the project costs each year (Secretary may waive or modify for hardship). Priority: Secretary must give priority to applicants that will implement evidence-based activities and that have demonstrated ability to prepare/develop principals who improved school-level outcomes, became principals in high-need schools, and remained principals in such schools for multiple years.

rubrics_metrics.name: School Leader Recruitment and Support — duration and extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration: grants are awarded for up to 5 years, with an optional 2-year extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-need school definition (program-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined here as elementary schools with at least 50 percent of enrolled students from families below the poverty line or secondary schools with at least 40 percent of enrolled students from families below the poverty line.

rubrics_metrics.name: STEM Master Teacher Corps — purpose and candidate identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: support efforts to develop and expand effective STEM professional development programs across a State and elevate the status of STEM teaching by recognizing, rewarding, attracting, and retaining outstanding STEM teachers, particularly in high-need and rural schools. States must identify candidates based on content knowledge, pedagogical knowledge, and success in teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Master teachers should be given opportunities to work in scholarly communities, lead high-quality PD, and receive additional compensation for contributions to improved teaching and learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter Schools Grants — purpose and program components
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: to support startup, replication, and expansion of high-quality charter schools (preK–12), improve access to facilities, and information dissemination and evaluation activities. Program components include State Entity Grants, Developer Grants, Credit Enhancement Grants, Facilities Grants, State Facilities Incentive Grants, CMO Grants, and National Activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter Schools Grants — eligible applicants by component
rubrics_metrics.description: Developer Grants: developers (individuals and public/private nonprofits) may apply directly to Secretary in States where no state entity received a grant. State Entity Grants: SEAs, State charter boards, governors, statewide charter support organizations. CMO Grants: nonprofit charter management organizations. Credit Enhancement Grants: public and private nonprofit entities assisting charter schools with financing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter Schools — use-of-funds and administrative caps
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must use not less than 90 percent of grant funds to make subgrants to charter school developers; not more than 3 percent of funds may be used for administrative costs; not less than 7 percent to provide technical assistance to developers and improve authorizing/oversight quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developers may use up to 18 months for planning/program design including hiring and compensating school leaders and instructional staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Facilities Incentive Grants — state law and cost-sharing conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: State eligibility: a State must establish or enhance and administer an aid program specified in State law providing annual financing on a per-pupil basis for charter school facilities. Duration and cost-sharing: awards up to 5 years, over which States pay an increasing share of program costs. States may partner with other organizations to provide up to 50 percent of the State share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter Schools — grant-making minimums and annual requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of grants: not less than 3. Secretary must make at least 3 new grants each year and fully fund the first 2 years of each grant with the initial award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnet Schools Assistance — eligible applicants under desegregation plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants: an LEA, or consortium of LEAs where appropriate, is eligible to receive a grant as part of a court-ordered, agency-ordered, or federally approved voluntary desegregation plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnet Schools — priority application criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary gives priority to applicants that: (1) demonstrate the greatest need for assistance; (2) propose to carry out new, evidence-based magnet programs, significantly revise existing programs using evidence-based methods, or replicate an existing magnet program with demonstrated record of success in increasing achievement and reducing racial isolation; (3) use methods other than academic examinations (such as a lottery) to admit students; and (4) increase racial integration by designing and implementing programs that would increase socioeconomic diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants that did not receive a grant the previous year receive priority for any funds appropriated above $75 million.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnet Schools — permissible uses and planning expenditure limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of funds: activities to improve academic achievement including planning/promotional activities, acquiring books/materials/equipment, and paying salaries of effective teachers and instructional personnel. Grantees may spend no more than 50 percent of project costs in the first year and 15 percent in the second and third years on planning activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds may be used to transport students enrolled in magnet schools provided transportation costs do not consume significant portion of award and strategy is sustainable after grant period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnet Schools — award duration and caps
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees receive awards for up to 5 years and may not receive more than $15 million over the course of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National reservation: Secretary may use up to 1 percent of funds for technical assistance and disseminating best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statewide Family Engagement Centers — eligible applicants and priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants: statewide organizations (or consortia). Priority: Secretary must give priority to centers that will use funds for evidence-based activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statewide Family Engagement Centers — national technical assistance reservation and minimum award
rubrics_metrics.description: National reservation for technical assistance: Secretary must reserve not more than 2 percent of funds to provide technical assistance by competitive grant or contract. Minimum grant award: Secretary must, to extent practicable, ensure a grant is awarded in an amount not less than $500,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statewide Family Engagement Centers — grantee funding usage requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees must use at least 65 percent of funds awarded in each fiscal year to serve LEAs, schools, and community-based organizations that serve high concentrations of disadvantaged students; and must use at least 30 percent of funds awarded each fiscal year to establish or expand technical assistance for evidence-based parent education programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education Innovation and Research (EIR) — tiered-evidence framework
rubrics_metrics.description: The program incorporates a tiered-evidence framework that supports larger awards for projects with the strongest evidence base and also supports early-stage promising projects willing to undergo rigorous evaluation: early-phase (development/feasibility), mid-phase (implementation and rigorous evaluation), and expansion/replication (scale-up of proven interventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early-phase grants focus on development and feasibility testing; mid-phase on implementation and evaluation; expansion on scaling interventions with sizable impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: EIR — eligible applicants and national reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants: LEAs, SEAs, BIE, consortia, nonprofit organizations, or partnerships with business, educational service agencies, or institutions of higher education. National reservation: Secretary may reserve up to 5 percent of program funds for technical assistance and dissemination of best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: EIR — rural set-aside
rubrics_metrics.description: At least 25 percent of funds appropriated for the program must be used for awards to serve rural areas, contingent on receiving enough applications of sufficient quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: EIR — matching requirement and waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees must provide matching funds equal to 10 percent of their grant award (in cash or in-kind) from Federal, State, local, or private sources. Secretary may waive this requirement on a case-by-case basis upon a showing of exceptional circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: EIR — evaluation and public reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All grantees must carry out a rigorous independent evaluation of the effectiveness of their project. Grantees are required to publicly report information about their projects, including number and percentage of children participating and progress on performance metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: EIR — required activities and planning funding proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Required activities: include planning to develop pipeline services, implementing pipeline services, and continuously evaluating and improving programs based on outcome data. Grantees must use at least 50 percent of their first-year awards, and at least 25 percent of their second-year awards, for planning activities to develop and implement pipeline services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duration: grants for not more than 5 years; may be extended up to 2 additional years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise Neighborhoods — purpose and eligible focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: to support distressed communities in implementing a comprehensive continuum of coordinated services to improve academic and developmental outcomes for children, youth, and families from birth through college, specifically in neighborhoods with high rates of poverty, childhood obesity, academic failure, and justice-system involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise Neighborhoods — priority and evidence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority applications: neighborhoods with schools implementing comprehensive or targeted improvement activities under Title I, Part A of ESEA; applicants that incorporate evidence-based activities into proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise Neighborhoods — matching requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Matching requirements: an amount equal to not less than 100 percent of the amount of the grant, and must come from Federal, State, local, and private sources. A portion of the matching funds must come from private sources, which may include in-kind contributions.
